liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer praises Black Peter as nice, and also singles out Easy Wind as righteous [4]
- **High Time** (1 review): Reviewer calls High Time perfect and rates the show highly on that song alone [4]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): Reviewer is struck that such a mellow tune can have so much punch, and that it invites fast dancing [9]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer singles out The Other One as great, with the rest of the show solid but not exceptional for the period [2]
- **Cosmic Charlie** (1 review): The Cosmic Charlie in the recording is cut, which the reviewer finds disappointing [3]

## The recordings

- **gd70-01-30.sbd.vernon.10546.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 93 min; rated 3.45/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound great and feels the show gets an unfair bad reputation; Reviewer finds the sound very good; Uploader hears a slight tinny, tunnel-like quality in the sound [1][4][9]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says this was Tom Constanten's last show with the band, followed by the band getting busted [3]
- Reviewer believes Tom Constanten's last show was actually 26 January 1970 in Honolulu, not this one [6]
- Reviewer says the band decided before the show that Constanten would leave; he played, and is buried in the mix [7]
- Constanten roomed with Pig when the bust happened that night; both escaped arrest, citing McNally page 352 [7]
- Reviewer says the band was busted on Bourbon Street later that evening, on the night the Warehouse opened [8]
- Reviewer says the sound was jinxed the next night, leading to a spontaneous acoustic set [8]
- Reviewer describes an opening of organized chaos, then a mellow groove alternating Pigpen and Jerry ballads and standards [9]
- Reviewer hears the band as tight and in sync, especially on the short songs [11]
- Points to the 24 January 1970 Honolulu soundboard as an excellent show from the Honolulu run with Constanten [6]
- Reviewer notes a Fleetwood Mac set from the same event also circulates and is awesome [7]
- Reviewer calls it an underrated, hidden gem of 1970 that stands up to the era's best [8]
- Reviewer says Cryptical reprises at the time usually ran only a few minutes, but this one went longer [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-01-30.sbd.vernon.10546.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke and Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Spectral analysis shows a sharp noise cutoff near 5kHz, suggesting signal processing somewhere in the lineage [1]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1970-01-30 Fri The Warehouse, New Orleans, LA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1115817834920/grateful-dead-1970-01-30-fri-the) [14]
